Comments: On April 29, 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection on the former location of the Corbett 3 well site in Derry Township, Westmoreland County.The following was observed during the inspection:No evidence of a fluid release to the surface, such as staining and/or distressed vegetation, was observed at approximate location of the plugged well. No debris and/or equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site (photo 4). The former access road and former well site have established greater than 70% vegetative growth coverage. No evidence of accelerated erosion and/or sedimentation was observed on site at the time of inspection. Minor evidence of vehicle traffic was observed through the former well site. However, the vegetative coverage on site does not appear to be adversely affected.The well site overall had already established 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage at the time of IR 4094628, the last surface inspection conducted on site on November 18, 2025. The Department recommended in IR 4094628 that the operator submit a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) no later than sixty (60) days after the date of IR 4094628, in accordance with PA Code 78.65(3). However, greater than sixty (60) days has elapsed since IR 4094628 was conducted, and the Department has not received a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator. Therefore, a violation shall be issued for failure to submit a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) within sixty (60) days after completing site restoration.Closure of this violation shall be contingent upon receiving an administratively complete Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/06/2023 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: K PETROLEUM INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/06/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8164680
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2023
Comments: On November 6 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking at a valve near the bottom of the tank, but did not appear to be actively leaking. Distressed vegetation was observed in an approximate 3 foot radius around the tank. Directly below the valve, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.15 mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. The readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading with readings of 0.25mS, 0.45mS, 0.39mS, and 0.46mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 3 foot radius around the production tank. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inform him of the release. Mr. Greco indicated that they had already replaced the faulty valve, and estimated the spill was roughly 15 barrels of production fluids and impacted the ground roughly 8 inches in depth. He stated remediation was scheduled to begin on 11/8/2023. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined, as well as how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/25/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 908943
Permit API: 015-23612
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/25/2021
Comments: On 02/25/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) Tanner & Hana location. The drilling of 3 wells commenced on location between the dates of 11/12/2020 – 11/13/2020. Drilling operations subsequently followed, were documented within inspection report # 3127696, and had recently finished. The purpose of this inspection was to document the current status of the site and to inspect the site for any indication of possible releases of regulated substances. I arrived onsite at 1335 hours. At the time of my arrival, there were 3 semi-trucks that were hauling timber matting and what appeared to be plastic corrugated pipe off location. There were an additional 11 vehicles parked around the edge of the pad, but no crew members were identified. The weather was 44 degrees with mostly sunny skies. The pad surface was mostly covered in puddles, as warm temperatures melted snow / ice cover. The containment berm and slopes around the site still had approximately 4 – 6 inches of snow cover present. The 3 newly drilled wells were inspected, and all appeared to have back pressure valves set (photo # 3). There appeared to be a thick and dark fluid within each of the well cellars (photo # 4, 5). The area immediately surrounding the wells appeared to have been recently regraded with crushed stone (photo # 6). Just west of the wells, an oily odor was noted. There appeared to be a containment liner still present on the pad surface, partially buried (photo # 7). Puddles on the pad surface around this area (noted in photo # 15) all appeared to have an oily sheen and oily odor (photo # 9, 10, 11). Black specks were present within most of the puddles, and a concentration of a dark substance was noted within a puddle (photo # 12, 13). Sample # 9544-044 was collected from a puddle along the NW edge of the site where both an oily odor and sheen were noted (photo # 14). The sample was collected for SAC 942 + Al, Br, Li analysis. The release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance to the pad surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a). Failure to report the release of an unknown quantity of a regulated substance is in violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.66(b)1. Violations have been cited against well permit # 015-23612. This release is referred to the DEP’s Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields. The department recommends: 1. Dewatering the pad surface. 2. Dewatering the well cellars. 3. Removing the tarp liner noted in photo # 7 I departed the site at 1419 hours.

Comments: On January 21 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Midas Well Pad (NOT previously approved on 10/28/2021) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/20/2026 (CTS 394728). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 4 total active wells on the well pad. Each well appeared equipped for production with a well tag present. No fluid leaks or spills were identified at the surface around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. The GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release occurred on 1/20/2026. He stated the release occurred from a hose failure on a portable heater onsite. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 10 gallons of glycol onto the graveled well pad.Mr. Miller stated remediation had been completed and all impacted gravel/material had been removed and placed into drums. The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 15 foot by 30 foot area adjacent to the portbale heater near the GPUs. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the release/remediation with readings of 0.04mS, 0.03mS, 0.06ms, and 0.04mS being obtained. These readings appeared comparable to the background reading of 0.03mS.Based on observations from this inspection and information provided by the operator, it appears that the spill has been remediated in accordance with current regulations. The Department requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Violations are being issued as immediately corrected.

Violation ID: 931499

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/24/2021
Comments: Inspection in response to a discharge of gas and crude oil from this well reported to the Department at 0250. The County HazMat Team and Department ERT were called to the incident and reported the incident as venting of crude oil and gas from a pressure relief valve on top of a tank. During the response, it was reported that the pump jack eventually stopped operating and the discharge of crude oil tapered off and essentially stopped. The valve continued to vent natural gas. The County HazMat Team strung caution tape around the well site, laid down pig matting where crude oil had sprayed and absorbent booms around the puddles of crude oil (Photos 1-8). Accompanying me during inspection is OGI Jon Shub (DEP) and Josh Boarts, the well tender for the operator. Boarts began clean up efforts by filling buckets with the oil that surrounded the well head and dumping it into the brine tank on site (Photo 9). Boarts then laid down pig matting around all affected areas and then absorb-it on the areas around the pump jack and well head (Photos 20-23). The spill was generally contained within the area of which the yellow tape is surrounding the site. The area around the well is flat aside from the depression around the pump jack that allowed the crude oil to pool around it. The closest Water of the Commonwealth is Deer Creek which is approximately 300 feet East of the well, but does not appear to be in danger of contamination due to the flat parking lot in which the well sits. According to the owner of the property, who has a video feed of the well, the discharge began at approximately 22:04 on 9/23. Oil had discharged up until the early morning when the HazMat team was on site. Josh Boarts estimated the spill to be around half a barrel while on site. The exact cause of why the pressure valve was released is unknown to the operator at this time, but the well tender Josh Boarts did say the valve is supposed to release at 250 lbs of pressure. Boarts was provided with the Department spill policy and program clarification memo. Boarts plans to gather visibly impacted material into large barrels before properly removing them off site.

Violation ID: 8186930
Permit API: 081-21938
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/08/2024
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted following a reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface from 3/1/24. A workover rig is in operation drilling out plugs on the well pad following fracing operations. Equipment for the frac has mostly been removed from the location. Additional equipment was being hauled away during this inspection. I met with EQT company man Marc McCartor at the beginning of this inspection. The area of the pad surface which was impacted by the 3/1/24 release appeared dry without any visible staining. Fluid is present in the stormwater channel along the northwest pad edge. The fluid is present in the channel from the approximate halfway point of the pad edge to the compost filter sock infiltration berm at the west corner of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid is 4.46 mS/cm near the halfway point of the pad edge. Approximately 25 feet west within the channel, the EC peaked at 10.23 mS/cm and then gradually decreased as it headed farther west within the channel. The EC of the fluid where the path of the fluid ended at the compost filter sock berm at the west corner is 2.43 mS/cm. I notified the company man about the elevated EC fluid in the stormwater channel and then took sample 0718-237 from the fluid in the stormwater channel at 1242. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I left a voicemail for EQT representative Rick Hall at 1338 on the same day to let him know of my findings. Later that day at 1555 I spoke with EQT representative Zac Subra. He told me that an internal investigation found that a contractor was flushing lines which had contained produced fluid following fracing operations. The contractor released what they believed to be freshwater which actually contained some portion of produced fluid. Mr. Subra said that they believe that this was the origin of the fluid in the channel and that EQT intends to pursue Act 2 remediation for this release. He also stated that a vacuum truck was already on site removing the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity. He said Penn E and R and Tobias Excavation was en route to the site to characterize and excavate the impacted material, respectively. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted for this release against permit 081-21946.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the 3/1/24 produced fluid release.

This well was spud on 8/18/2011, all submitted production reports for this well since that time indicate that the well has not been produced. The site ID sign for this well site is located at the end of the spur road that leads to this well. This sign does not meet the requirements of 78a.55(4). The access road leading to this well site is in suitable condition for the limited traffic that is currently using it. Maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to the West Branch of the Clarion River. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site and the access road banks appears to be established, future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site.

Comments: I conducted a routine inspection of the Allshouse Fraser 1001 well, this well was stimulated yesterday. Accelerated erosion of the road surface is taking place, a spring run with steady flow is present and running down the road due to lack of a culvert or other BMP to carry the water across the road. The spring left the road ditch and ran down the road approximately 300 feet before reentering a road ditch. The sediment laden water then traveled through a cross culvert before being discharged over the hillside above Route 6. The water then ran an additional 200 feet over the hillside and into the storm drain on the east bound lane of Route 6. From there the sediment laden water continued to the storm sewer outfall above the river and entered into the Allegheny River. The plume of sediment water remained for approximately 30 feet along the south bank of the Allegheny River.

Secondary containment has been installed onsite in location of the GPU units (see photo 10). A crane is onsite to move the GPU units into the newly-installed secondary containment (see photos 9 and 11). This is being conducted per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department. The rolloff boxes that were present during the time of IR 3969681 appear to have been removed from site. No visual evidence of any remaining impacted material was observed in the formerly impacted area.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that visual remediation of the impacted area has been successfully completed. However, violations issued from IR 3969681 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of this release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program at the time of this inspection.

Violation ID: 8184829

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On June 2 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Swiantek 3 OG Well.The findings were as follows: The purpose of this inspection was to respond a brine release that was reported to the Department at 10:00am that occurred on June 2 2023. Penneco stated that there was no release evident during a site visit Monday May 29 2023 but the release was found June 2. No specific time frame on when the release occurred on June 2 is available at this time. The Department is requesting Penneco provide the time at which the release was discovered on June 2, 2023 and by who, to be included in the NOV response. The Department arrived at the well pad at approximately 11:00am.The Department contacted Penneco representative Marc Jacobs via telephone, who proceeded to explain how the spill occurred. Mr. Jacobs explained that shut off valve at the base of the production tank was knocked off. This caused the brine tank to release approximately 30 barrels of brine into the neighboring agricultural field. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area in accordance with the Department Spill Policy.The Department also request written clarification from the Operator on how the quantity released was determined by June 14 2023. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the spill site in 5 places throughout the neighboring agricultural field. Soil conductivity readings at the spill site were 7.28mS, 8.18mS, 1.89mS, 6.11mS, and 4.55mS respectively. Visible distressed vegetation extended from base of production tank downslope into agricultural field approximately 158 ft. At the time of the inspection,The well appeared equipped for production. The access road appeared to be stabilized at the time of this inspection. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The well posting was present at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations will be issued. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests when available. The Department will conduct a subsequent inspection to continue to evaluate remediation of this spill.

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 998054
Permit API: 051-21279
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Perry Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/02/2023
Comments: On June 2 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Swiantek 3 OG Well.The findings were as follows: The purpose of this inspection was to respond a brine release that was reported to the Department at 10:00am that occurred on June 2 2023. Penneco stated that there was no release evident during a site visit Monday May 29 2023 but the release was found June 2. No specific time frame on when the release occurred on June 2 is available at this time. The Department is requesting Penneco provide the time at which the release was discovered on June 2, 2023 and by who, to be included in the NOV response. The Department arrived at the well pad at approximately 11:00am.The Department contacted Penneco representative Marc Jacobs via telephone, who proceeded to explain how the spill occurred. Mr. Jacobs explained that shut off valve at the base of the production tank was knocked off. This caused the brine tank to release approximately 30 barrels of brine into the neighboring agricultural field. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the area in accordance with the Department Spill Policy.The Department also request written clarification from the Operator on how the quantity released was determined by June 14 2023. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the spill site in 5 places throughout the neighboring agricultural field. Soil conductivity readings at the spill site were 7.28mS, 8.18mS, 1.89mS, 6.11mS, and 4.55mS respectively. Visible distressed vegetation extended from base of production tank downslope into agricultural field approximately 158 ft. At the time of the inspection,The well appeared equipped for production. The access road appeared to be stabilized at the time of this inspection. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The well posting was present at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations will be issued. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests when available. The Department will conduct a subsequent inspection to continue to evaluate remediation of this spill.

The soils in a 2' radius around the failed connected were tested and gas was detected at a peak of 31%LEL in the soils at 3" depth. No 2023 APR is on record, the latest record is from 2022 and indicates production. No 2023 MIA is on record, the latest record is from 2022. Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 6/9/2026, a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection (CTS #: 398384) of STL Resources LLCs Kjelgaard 802 multi-well pad located in Gaines Township, Tioga County. Upon arrival to the site at 0915 hours, weather was 72F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).No fluids were observed on the pad surface field.This inspection was conducted in response to a release of approximately 15 gallons of produced fluids onto the pad surface from a pressure relief valve on 6/8/2026 at 1100 hours, STL immediately reported this incident to the DEP (photo #2). Upon arrival to the site, the impacted pad material had already been scraped and removed from the site and hauled to WM Phoenix Resources Landfill in Wellsboro for disposal. I screened soils in this area for electrical conductivity which ranged from ~130-500us/cm.There are 3 wells tagged with American Petroleum Institute (API) numbers located onsite, a workover rig was also observed performing well maintenance (photos #7 and 8). 3 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #9). The GPUs do not utilize any visible secondary containment structures. A steel double-walled produced fluids tank is located onsite (photo #10); this tank utilizes an integrated secondary containment structure. A temporary storage tank was observed onsite and is currently in use for well maintenance activities (photo #11). The area surrounding the site remains permanently stabilized with greater than 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. No post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls are installed onsite.Based on the findings of this inspection, the following violations are noted against API #: 117-20185 and have been immediately corrected due to STL Resources immediate remediation and removal of the impacted pad material:-25 PA 78a.57(a)-35 P.S. 691.402(b)-35 P.S. 6018.301No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1015 hours.
